output.brief: The gap is mostly a time-in-level effect, not an office-attendance effect. Remote hiring only opened to all roles in July 2024, so most remote staff are new: 230 of 340 are not yet eligible under the 18-month rule, against 200 of 760 office staff. Among eligible staff, nomination rates (28.6% vs 28.2%), approval rates (73.8% vs 71.0%) and promotion rates (21.1% vs 20.0%) are nearly equal. Applying office rates to the remote eligibility mix predicts 8.2%, against the 7.6% observed. Remote staff also leave no faster than office staff (10.9% vs 11.6%). The eligible remote group is small (110), so a modest real gap can't be ruled out. Proximity effects on stretch work remain untested; the manager interviews hint at it, but there's no data. I'm fairly confident (about 75–85%). Don't announce the three-day office rule. It would target the wrong cause and hit about 180 staff hired on home-based contracts. Instead, change reporting to compare eligible staff only, and re-check at FY2027. Optionally, start collecting assignment data, and brief staff on promotion criteria, since only 41% of remote staff say they understand them.
